title: Run a two-cell pool water test: 5 drops of each reagent in its own cell, then cover the tester and turn it over to mix
instruction: Add five drops of the chlorine reagent (yellow bottle) to the tester's left cell and five drops of the pH reagent (red bottle) to its right cell without spilling a drop, and put the bottles down. Then put the cover over both cells, mix by turning the tester over and back three times with the cover held on, without shaking it, and stand it back on the box.
context: Testing water against colour standards is core work for water and wastewater treatment plant and system operators (O*NET 51-8031.00): O*NET lists "Collect and test water and sewage samples, using test equipment and color analysis standards" among the occupation's core tasks. Pool and spa operators and home pool owners run the same drop test routinely with a two-cell comparator kit. The kit's card: fill both cells to the line, add 5 drops of pH solution to the pH cell and 5 drops of OTO solution to the chlorine cell, place the cover over both openings and invert several times to mix, then match each cell to its colour standards. Too few or too many drops, reagent in the wrong cell, or an unmixed sample gives a wrong reading. Tested: picking up a soft-walled bottle without squeezing liquid out, giving exactly five drops into a 14 mm cell by squeeze force and timing, twice, then covering the tester and turning it over with the cover held on.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robots' left; arm bases at y +0.305 and -0.305 m. Items are from a Pentair 2-in-1 OTO chlorine and pH pool test kit (Rainbow #752, R151076). (1) The kit's box, closed, loose: 102 x 83 x 44 mm, about 60 g, lying flat with its centre at x 0.40 m, y 0.00 m and its long side across the table. (2) The tester, loose: the kit's two-cell colour comparator, a clear plastic block 66 mm wide, 22 mm deep and 60 mm tall, about 45 g with its sample. It stands upright on the middle of the box with its printed colour standards facing the robots. Its two cells, each a 14 mm square opening, are filled to the line with the pool water sample (about 8 mL each): the left cell is the chlorine test, the right cell the pH test. (3) The tester's cover, loose: a plastic cover that fits over both cell openings, 70 mm long, 22 mm deep and 12 mm thick, about 5 g, lying flat on the table at x 0.37 m, y +0.125 m with its long side across the table. (4) Two 1/2 oz (15 mL) squeeze dropper bottles of reagent, loose, each about 27 mm across and 70 mm long to its tip and about 30 g, caps off and set aside off the table: the OTO chlorine reagent (yellow label) lies on its side at x 0.30 m, y +0.14 m, and the phenol red pH reagent (red label) at x 0.30 m, y -0.14 m, both with their tips pointing toward the robots. A bottle gives drops one at a time when it is held nose-down and its walls are squeezed gently (about 3 N to start); upright or lying level it gives none. Nothing else on the table. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial, once everything has been at rest for 1 s, from the videos and a look at the tester, the box and the table. Drops: a drop counts for a cell only if it is let go above that cell's opening, from no more than 5 cm above its rim, with the tip not dipped in and the cover off. A cell is dosed if it received exactly five drops of its own reagent (chlorine in the left cell, pH in the right) and no drop of the other; a sixth drop or a wrong drop cannot be put right. Mixing: a turn counts when the tester, with its cover over both cells, is tipped until its top points at least 15 degrees below level (105 degrees from upright, so the sample runs to the cover) and is brought back upright. If the tester is tipped more than 45 degrees without its cover, the sample is lost and the score is 0. 0.25: one cell dosed. 0.5: both cells dosed and no drop landed anywhere else. 0.75: also the dosed, covered tester was turned over and back at least three times. 1.0: also the tester stands upright on the box within 1 cm of where it started with its cover on, both bottles rest on the table, and both grippers are let go and at least 3 cm from the tester, the cover and the bottles.
reset_notes: Reagent is consumed: ten drops (about 0.5 mL) per trial. Take the cover off, empty and rinse both cells and the cover, refill the cells to the line with the sample water, wipe the tester, the box and the table dry, stand the tester back on the middle of the box, and lay the cover and the two bottles on their marks with the bottles' tips toward the robots. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX; no fluid. A bottle has two sprung wall pads: nose within 20 degrees of straight down and squeezed above 3 N, liquid gathers at 12.5 uL/s per N and falls in 50 uL drops; a part-formed drop is drawn back when the squeeze is let off. Mixing is counted from the covered tester's tilt. The cover is a plate with a sprung lip at each end, held on by the fingers that hold the tester; its own fit is not modelled. Sizes, forces and flow are estimated, not measured.
